run.training: LoRA r16 a32, two epochs over 364 rows: 258 clean distillation rows plus 106 in-interval positives and same-video out-of-interval hard negatives from the licensed pilot's train split
run.held_out: 196 rows: the 58-row production slice (coffee fixtures plus every tenth window) and 138 rows from the licensed pilot's untouched test split

comparison_to_shakedown.verification_status_agreement: 0.611 on 18 rows to 0.776 on 156 rows (+16.5 points, the direct effect of hard-negative training)

verdict: The hard-negative training delivered a measured quality gain exactly where the system gates everything: verification calls now agree with the hosted teacher on three of four cases across a 156-row gate, at perfect schema validity, from a pinned 4B local model. Agreement is measured against the hosted teacher's recorded statuses, not human ground truth; the decisive comparison against the hosted model on untouched data is the frozen stage-7 benchmark protocol (research/untouched-benchmark-design-2026-11-20.md).
limits: Status agreement is teacher-relative, not ground-truth accuracy.
The pilot's test videos appear in evaluation only; the pre-inference contamination audit in the stage-7 protocol governs any external claim.
One held-out split; word overlap is a coarse similarity, not correctness.
